Cases.Name: SQL
Cases.Prompt:
Write a detailed technical explanation of how a relational database executes
a SELECT query. Cover parsing, query planning, indexes, joins, sorting,
transactions, and returning results. Use several paragraphs and examples.

Cases.Name: CSharp
Cases.Prompt:
Implement a C# async method that reads one length-prefixed UTF-8 message from
a NetworkStream. The prefix is an unsigned 32-bit big-endian byte length.
Reject payloads larger than 1 MiB before allocating them. Handle partial reads,
EOF before a frame, EOF inside a frame, zero-length payloads, invalid UTF-8,
and cancellation. Do not dispose the caller's stream. State the method's
return and exception contract, provide the code, and explain five edge cases.

Cases.Name: Summary
Cases.Prompt:
Summarize the following fictional incident report for an engineering review.
Use four sections: timeline, confirmed cause, contributing factors, and actions.
Keep facts distinct from hypotheses. Include all numerical impact figures and
assignments. Explain why the proposed actions address the observed failure.
Do not invent measurements or claim that an untested action is effective.

At 09:05 a cache configuration change set all product keys to expire at 09:15.
At 09:15 the request rate remained 120 requests/second, but database reads
rose from 40 to 960 queries/second. Application CPU remained below 55 percent.
The connection pool reached its limit of 100 connections. Request p95 rose
from 180 milliseconds to 4.8 seconds. Between 09:15 and 09:22, 840 requests
returned HTTP 503. There was no confirmed data loss or unauthorized access.
At 09:18 the on-call engineer rolled back the configuration. This did not
restore already expired cache entries. At 09:22 a controlled cache warm-up
finished and p95 returned to 190 milliseconds. Logs showed many concurrent
loads for the same 20 product IDs. The database team found no failed database
nodes. Synchronized expiration and duplicate loads are the confirmed trigger
and amplification mechanism. Network packet loss was suggested but not measured.
Mira will add per-key request coalescing by Tuesday. Oleh will introduce TTL
jitter by Wednesday. Both changes require load tests before deployment.
The team rejected simply doubling the connection pool without measuring
database capacity. A proposed stale-cache fallback still needs a review of
which product fields can safely be served stale. Follow-up tests must cover
simultaneous expiration, backend timeouts, failed loads, and recovery.
